items.title: vLLM Day-0 Support for ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview: Plugin Deployment and E2E Inference Acceleration
items.summary_1line: Baidu's ERNIE team and vLLM add day-0 support for ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview, a 280B-parameter MoE model with 14B activated per token, via the vllm-ERNIE plugin installed alongside vllm==0.32.0.
items.editor_note: Shows a model lab shipping launch-day serving support as a vLLM plugin pinned to a specific vLLM release.

items.title: Can agents write inference engines from scratch in 12 hours and beat vLLM?
items.summary_1line: Humanity's Last System (HLS) is an open benchmark where coding agents get live GPU sandboxes for up to 36 hours to build specialized inference servers, which are then verified and scored for speed against vLLM-style baselines.
items.editor_note: Turns vLLM into the benchmark target for agent-written inference engines.

editorial.tldr: This is a theme thread, not one event: three separate items treat vLLM as the default open serving stack. It opened with Warmctl, a Show HN tool for faster vLLM cold starts, then vLLM shipped day-0 support for Baidu's ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview through a plugin.
editorial.whats_new: Humanity's Last System (HLS), an open benchmark, gives coding agents live GPU sandboxes for up to 36 hours to build inference servers, then verifies them and scores their speed against vLLM-style baselines.
editorial.why_it_matters: vLLM is now the reference point for serving: new models ship as vLLM plugins, tools patch its cold starts, and agent benchmarks measure themselves against it.
editorial.take_for_builders: For ERNIE 5.5 Flash, pin vllm==0.32.0 with the vllm-ERNIE plugin. Treat HLS results as research until verified scores beat your own vLLM baseline on your models.
